atomic_findings.behavior_claim: At python-attrs/attrs commit d2fbfccc1ce77dcc927a86eae9521c95dc4e289c, for a slotted chain A (attrs, on_setattr=setters.frozen) -> non-attrs B(A) -> mutable slotted attrs C(B), _create_slots_class() checks only self._cls.__bases__ for __attrs_own_setattr__ in each base's own __dict__; B.__dict__ carries neither the marker nor __setattr__, so C is not reset to object.__setattr__ and C(1).x = 2 dispatches to A's attrs-generated frozen setter, raising attr.exceptions.FrozenAttributeError. Closed by the pinned source's immediate-base loop and XXX comment plus the project's executable xfail reproducer test_slotted_confused (xfail raises=attr.exceptions.FrozenAttributeError) in SOURCE_EXCERPT.py; the dict-backed contrast matches the test docstring and the getattr-based MRO-visible check in _patch_original_class.
atomic_findings.regression_test: Response bytes [3307,3548): un-xfail the confused-chain contract for both slots=False and slots=True — given A slotted attrs with on_setattr=setters.frozen, transparent non-attrs B(A), and mutable attrs C(B): C(1).x = 2 succeeds, C.__setattr__ is object.__setattr__, and C.__attrs_own_setattr__ is False; paired with the preservation row [3873,4054): when B(A) defines a user __setattr__, both slot modes preserve B.__setattr__ with no reset. Uses only existing attrs API (attr.s, attr.ib, on_setattr, setters.frozen, __attrs_own_setattr__, object.__setattr__); expected results replicate the already-asserted reset contract of test_setattr_reset_if_no_custom_setattr, the passing test_setattr_inherited_do_not_reset preservation contract, and the intended behavior stated in the test_slotted_confused docstring — no invented API or contract.
atomic_findings.residue: When inherited behavior carries an ownership marker, decide whether to remove it by locating the effective method provider first (first class in MRO attribute-resolution order whose own __dict__ contains the method), then read the ownership marker from that same provider's own namespace; never continue past a user-owned provider. Falsifiable per response bytes [5824,6007): any hierarchy where this rule selects a different provider than Python's actual __setattr__ lookup, or replaces an effective user-owned setter, disproves it. The rule is consistent with every executable case in the packet (test_slotted_confused intended behavior, test_setattr_inherited_do_not_reset, test_setattr_reset_if_no_custom_setattr, test_slotted_class_can_have_custom_setattr).
atomic_findings.applicability_predicate: Applies only to class machinery where method ownership is reliably represented in the method-defining class's own __dict__ (here __attrs_own_setattr__ set by attrs on classes whose __setattr__ it generates) and where the effective method is resolved by ordinary class-dictionary/MRO lookup (response bytes [6009,6334)).
exclusions: methods or ownership markers mutated independently after class creation
__setattr__ supplied dynamically by a metaclass without an owning class-dictionary entry
attribute resolution mechanisms not represented by ordinary class-dictionary/MRO lookup
multiple-inheritance orderings beyond packet test coverage are proposed boundary tests, not closed contract
